about: Parse trees from parseQuery. input is the query string. expected is the tree, or null when there is nothing to search for. matchCase defaults to false.

cases.name: only spaces
cases.note: Nothing to search for. The search view shows nothing; an empty graph colour group matches every node.

cases.name: a stray closing paren
cases.note: A stray ) is skipped.

cases.name: ORANGE is a word
cases.note: OR is the operator only as a whole word, and a trailing OR is dropped.

cases.name: an unclosed quote
cases.note: An unclosed quote runs to the end of the query.

cases.name: an unclosed paren
cases.note: An unclosed ( closes at the end of the query.

cases.name: only a closing paren
cases.note: A stray ) is skipped, so this is nothing to search for.

cases.name: a closing bracket outside a property
cases.note: ] ends a word only inside a property, so on its own it is the word ].

cases.name: OR at the start
cases.note: A leading OR is dropped.

cases.name: OR at the end
cases.note: A trailing OR is dropped.

cases.name: OR beside OR
cases.note: An empty OR arm is dropped.

cases.name: negated OR
cases.note: Negating the OR token is dropped, so there is nothing to search for.

cases.name: a dash alone
cases.note: A dash at the end of the query is the word -, not a negation.

cases.name: a dash before a space
cases.note: A dash before a space is the word -.

cases.name: an upper-case operator
cases.note: Operator names are matched in any case.

cases.name: an unknown operator
cases.note: An unknown operator is one word. Grove has no regex search, so /abc/ is a word too.

cases.name: task: is a word
cases.note: Grove has no task: operator; this is the word task:x. Obsidian's search help (help.obsidian.md/plugins/search) lists task:, block: and section:. No Obsidian result is recorded; that page was not re-checked for this corpus.

cases.name: slashes are not a regex
cases.note: A slash-wrapped word is not a regex.

cases.name: a negated term in an operator group
file: inside line:
cases.note: Parsed as a line group whose term is file:. A file term is not looked up in the text, so the group matches no line.

cases.name: an empty tag
cases.note: The # is stripped after the empty check, so the term's text is empty. It is not null. No stored tag is under an empty name, so a search matches nothing.

cases.name: a tag with a slash
cases.note: A tag term is lower case and loses one leading #.

cases.name: slashes trimmed off a path
cases.note: Leading and trailing slashes are stripped off a path term.

cases.name: a path that is only a slash
cases.note: The slash is stripped after the empty check, so the term's text is empty. It is not null. Every path contains the empty string, so a search matches every file.

cases.name: an empty path quote
cases.note: The quoted path is empty, so there is nothing to search for.

cases.name: a property value that is a group
a property closed by an inner bracket
cases.note: The inner property clears the in-property state, so the ] after d is part of the word d].

cases.name: a wikilink is not a property
cases.note: A second [ is not a property, and ] does not end a word outside one, so this is one word.

cases.name: a property with an empty key
cases.note: The key trims to empty, so the property is dropped and there is nothing to search for.

cases.name: NUL inside the query
cases.note: The top-level group stops at U+0000, so only a is read. b is never parsed.

cases.name: a tab between words
cases.note: A tab is whitespace, so this is two terms.

cases.name: an ideographic space between words
cases.note: U+3000 is whitespace, so this is two terms.

cases.name: a BOM trimmed off a term
cases.note: U+FEFF is whitespace and trim removes it, so the term is alpha.

cases.name: match case still lowers a tag
cases.note: Tag text is lower case even with Match case. The property key is too; the value stays as typed.

cases.name: match case lowers the key only
cases.note: The property key is lower case. The value stays as typed.
